chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from one of his companions, from Al-Husayn ibn Hazim, from Husayn ibn Umar ibn Yazeed, from his father who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The one who slanders his brother regarding his Religion, so there is no sanctity between the two of them; and the one who deals with his brother with the like of what the people deal with him, so he is disavowed from what he is impersonating'.
ai.seo_question: What is the consequence of slandering a Muslim brother in his religion according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to establish the foundational Shia ethic of 'sahl al-zann' (assuming the best), warning that accusing a fellow Muslim of religious deficiency severs the spiritual bond of 'hurmah'. The second part clarifies that reciprocal treatment with the general public ('al-nas') serves as a safeguard against the specific charge of hypocrisy, distinguishing ordinary social reciprocity from the deeper, often hidden, faults of the pretender.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from one of his companions, from Al Husayn Bin Hazim, from Husayn Bin Umar Bin Yazeed, from his father who said,

‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘The one who slanders his brother regarding his Religion, so there would be no sanctity between the two of them; and the one who deals with his brother with the like of what the people deal with him, so he would be disavowed from what he is impersonating’.
en.sarwar: 2. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from certain individuals of his people from al-Husayn ibn Hazim from Husayn ibn ‘Umar ibn Yazid from his father who has said the following:

“I heard abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) saying, ‘Whenever one accuses his brother (in belief) in his religious matters, religious relations will cease to exist between them. Whoever deals with his brother (in belief) just as he deals with other people, his religious relations (religious brotherhood) toward him all comes apart.’”
